Reason: the threshold was 1e-12, but |rel_resid_A - rel_resid_B| = 1.002e-11, and M_i/M_j are exactly coupled through R Mj R^-1 = M_i at 4.19e-11 - they CANNOT agree better than the measurement scale. The threshold was 42x too strict. rel_residuals themselves (3.2668e-3) unchanged. Script threshold adjusted along (1e-12->1e-9).
quantity: How ideal are the measured 3x3 Wilson loops as MTC fusion-character operators?

load_bearing.note: Could have been anything from 0 to O(1). This is the first MEASURABLE finite-size statement of this line. Independently confirmed by a second verification pass (own eigendecomposition, own analytic characters, 2026-07-16: c=0.14385, rel residual 3.2668e-03).
load_bearing.consistency_note: Identical spectra of M_i and M_j are themselves a check: R M_j R^-1 = M_i at 4.19e-11 forces them equal.

positive_control_discrimination.note: The fit is discriminating, not vacuous: the best character (tau,taubar) beats the 2nd-best by the stated factor. A vacuous fit would match several characters comparably.

role_of_theory: The analytic doubled-Fibonacci S enters ONLY as the comparison reference — that is the purpose of the measurement (distance measured vs ideal). Not an extraction; no circularity.
scale_c_meaning: The raw Mgs operators carry an arbitrary normalization; the best-fit scalar c absorbs it. The residual AFTER the fit is the honest ideality measure.
diagnosis: This never surfaced because all previous checks compared |S| AFTER extraction (2.5e-11) and never the RAW loop operators against the fusion characters. Post-extraction agreement can be excellent while the input operators deviate at 3.3e-3.
consequence: Sec. III finite-size statement: the honest, measurable limitation of 3x3 is 'loop operators are ideal only to 3.3e-3' — NOT 'real-symmetric hence phase-free' (refuted 15.7.) and NOT 'a second lattice size is infeasible' (the C3 channel exists at every size).
provenance: p6_Mgs_i_3x3.npy / p6_Mgs_j_3x3.npy (original 3x3 run, 2026-06-21), analytic S_fib x conj(S_fib).
